26002-linda-tressel.title: Linda Tressel
26002-linda-tressel.creator: Anthony Trollope
26002-linda-tressel.description: A book by Anthony Trollope. that its people and its manners were as strange to him as though he had gone beyond the reach of his own mother-tongue. But here he had married, and from Cologne had brought home his bride to the picturesque, red, gabled house by the water's side in his own city.

arxiv-2103-06484.title: Robust High-Speed Running for Quadruped Robots via Deep Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2103-06484.creator: Guillaume Bellegarda, Yiyu Chen, Zhuochen Liu, Quan Nguyen
arxiv-2103-06484.description: Abstract Deep reinforcement learning has emerged as a popular and powerful way to develop locomotion controllers for quadruped robots. Common approaches have largely focused on learning actions directly in joint space, or learning to modify and offset foot positions produced by trajectory generators.

arxiv-2108-07989.title: Asymptotic behavior of least energy solutions to the Finsler Lane-Emden problem with large exponents
arxiv-2108-07989.creator: Sadaf Habibi 1, Futoshi Takahashi 2
arxiv-2108-07989.description: Abstract . In this paper we are concerned with the least energy solutions to the Lane-Emden problem driven by an anisotropic operator, so-called the Finsler N N -Laplacian, on a bounded domain in ℝ N \mathbb{R}^{N} . We prove several asymptotic formulae as the nonlinear exponent gets large.

arxiv-2201-07459.title: PT4AL: Using Self-Supervised Pretext Tasks for Active Learning
arxiv-2201-07459.creator: John Seon Keun Yi, Minseok Seo, Jongchan Park, Dong-Geol Choi
arxiv-2201-07459.description: Abstract Labeling a large set of data is expensive. Active learning aims to tackle this problem by asking to annotate only the most informative data from the unlabeled set. We propose a novel active learning approach that utilizes self-supervised pretext tasks and a unique data sampler to select data that are both difficult and representative.

arxiv-2402-10784.title: Simultaneous symmetry breaking in spontaneous Floquet states: Floquet-Nambu-Goldstone modes, Floquet thermodynamics, and the time operator
arxiv-2402-10784.creator: Juan Ramón Muñoz de Nova, Fernando Sols
arxiv-2402-10784.description: Abstract We study simultaneous symmetry-breaking in a spontaneous Floquet state, focusing on the specific case of an atomic condensate. We first describe the quantization of the Nambu-Goldstone (NG) modes for a stationary state simultaneously breaking several symmetries of the Hamiltonian by invoking the generalized Gibbs ensemble, which enables a thermodynamical description of the problem.

arxiv-2408-02815.title: Entanglement Holonomy for Photon Pairs in Curved Spacetime
arxiv-2408-02815.creator: Mark T. Lusk
arxiv-2408-02815.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mark T. Lusk. Polarization holonomy is analytically determined for maximally entangled photon pairs that transit a class of closed trajectories in the Kerr metric. This is used to define and investigate an entanglement holonomy not associated with constituent product states. I Introduction Since the seminal work of Pancharatnam almost seventy years ago Pancharatnam_1956 , electromagnetic radiation has provided an ideal setting for the exploration of holonomy.

arxiv-2410-19751.title: Fitting the seven-parameter Generalized Tempered Stable distribution to the financial data
arxiv-2410-19751.creator: Aubain Nzokem, Daniel Maposa
arxiv-2410-19751.description: Abstract The paper proposes and implements a methodology to fit a seven-parameter Generalized Tempered Stable (GTS) distribution to financial data. The nonexistence of the mathematical expression of the GTS probability density function makes the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) inadequate for providing parameter estimations.

arxiv-2503-12913.title: A Block-Sparse Bayesian Learning Algorithm with Dictionary Parameter Estimation for Multi-Sensor Data Fusion Thanks: This project was partly funded by the Christian Doppler Laboratory for Location-aware Electronic Systems.
arxiv-2503-12913.creator: Jakob Möderl ∗ , Anders Malte Westerkam † , Alexander Venus ∗ , and Erik Leitinger ∗
arxiv-2503-12913.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jakob Möderl ∗ , Anders Malte Westerkam † , Alexander Venus ∗ , and Erik Leitinger ∗. We propose an sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) -based method that leverages group sparsity and multiple parameterized dictionaries to detect the relevant dictionary entries and estimate their continuous parameters by combining data from multiple independent sensors. In a MIMO multi-radar setup, we demonstrate its effectiveness in jointly detecting and localizing multiple objects, while also emphasizing its broader applicability to various signal processing tasks.

arxiv-2503-22194.title: Origen : Zero-Shot 3D Orientation Grounding in Text-to-Image Generation
arxiv-2503-22194.creator: Yunhong Min Daehyeon Choi Kyeongmin Yeo Jihyun Lee Minhyuk SungKAIST
arxiv-2503-22194.description: Abstract We introduce Origen , the first zero-shot method for 3D orientation grounding in text-to-image generation across multiple objects and diverse categories. While previous work on spatial grounding in image generation has mainly focused on 2D positioning, it lacks control over 3D orientation.

arxiv-2508-02241.title: Isolating Culture Neurons in Multilingual Large Language Models
arxiv-2508-02241.creator: Danial Namazifard, Lukas Galke
arxiv-2508-02241.description: Abstract Language and culture are deeply intertwined, yet it is so far unclear how and where multilingual large language models encode culture. Here, we extend upon an established methodology for identifying language-specific neurons and extend it to localize and isolate culture-specific neurons, carefully disentangling their overlap and interaction with language-specific neurons.

arxiv-2511-18824.title: Assessing the alignment between infants’ visual and linguistic experience using multimodal language models
arxiv-2511-18824.description: Abstract Figuring out which objects or concepts words refer to is a central language learning challenge for young children. Most models of this process posit that children learn early object labels from co-occurrences of words and their referents that occur when someone around them talks about an object in the immediate physical environment.

arxiv-2512-07269.title: A graph generation pipeline for critical infrastructures based on heuristics, images and depth data
arxiv-2512-07269.creator: Mike Diessner, Yannick Tarant
arxiv-2512-07269.description: Abstract Virtual representations of physical critical infrastructures, such as water or energy plants, are used for simulations and digital twins to ensure resilience and continuity of their services. These models usually require 3D point clouds from laser scanners that are expensive to acquire and require specialist knowledge to use.

arxiv-2604-15934.title: Reweighting Estimators for Density Response in Path Integral Monte Carlo: Applications to linear, nonlinear and cross-species density response

openalex-w2010581199.title: UNEP-SETAC guideline on global land use impact assessment on biodiversity and ecosystem services in LCA
openalex-w2010581199.creator: Thomas Koellner, Laura de Baan, Tabea Beck, Miguel Brandão, Bárbara María Civit, Manuele D. Margni, Llorenç Milà i Canals, Rosie Saad, Danielle Maia de Souza, Ruedi Müller‐Wenk
openalex-w2010581199.source: OpenAlex / The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
openalex-w2010581199.description: As a consequence of the multi-functionality of land, the impact assessment of land use in Life Cycle Impact Assessment requires the modelling of several impact pathways covering biodiversity and ecosystem services. To provide consistency amongst these separate impact pathways,...

pmc-11289835.title: Bladder cancer with bone marrow metastases and thrombotic microangiopathy: a case report
pmc-11289835.creator: Khder Yousf, Nagham Daoud, Ali Habib, Rabab Salloum, Firas Hussein
pmc-11289835.description: Bladder cancer is one of the most common cancers of the urinary tract and the 10th most common cancer worldwide according to the World Health Organization (WHO), with a higher incidence in men than in women. Bladder cancer rarely presents with a clinical picture of bone marrow infiltration which may result in thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA).

pmc-11496868.title: Association between serum neuron-specific enolase at admission and the risk of delayed neuropsychiatric sequelae in adults with carbon monoxide poisoning: A meta-analysis
pmc-11496868.creator: Yu Zhang, Nan Gao, Yingbo Wang, Wenxin Hu, Zhihao Wang, Li Pang
pmc-11496868.description: Delayed neuropsychiatric sequelae (DNS) significantly impact the quality of life in patients following acute carbon monoxide poisoning (COP). This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the relationship between serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE) levels at admission and the risk of DNS in adults after acute COP.

pmc-11568893.title: Alois Alzheimer (1864-1915): The Father of Modern Dementia Research and the Discovery of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11568893.creator: Vishwa S Thakor, Anisha Tyagi, James M Lee Jr., Frederick Coffman, Rahul Mittal
pmc-11568893.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Alois Alzheimer was a German psychologist and neuropathologist who significantly advanced the study of dementia with his discovery of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Based on his assessment of a 51-year-old female patient with symptoms of presenile dementia and after conducting a postmortem autopsy of her brain, Alzheimer distinguished two neurological substances - senile plaques and neurofibrillary tangles - as unique markers of what was later deemed as AD.

pmc-11612664.title: Uptake of Risk‐Reducing Salpingo‐Oophorectomy and Gynaecologic Surveillance Among Germline BRCA Pathogenic Variants Carriers
pmc-11612664.creator: Alessandra Inzoli, Serena Negri, Cristina Dell'Oro, Clarissa Costa, Liliana Marchetta, Mariaclara Boccadutri, Simona Fumagalli, Gaia Roversi, Elena Maria Sala, Chiara Celi, Valentina Rossi, Robert Fruscio
pmc-11612664.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionRisk‐reducing salpingo‐oophorectomy (RRSO) is recommended by international guidelines in women with BRCA1/2 germline pathogenic variants (PV) to prevent ovarian cancer. Despite the solid recommendation, women frequently refuse surgery and uptake rates reported in the literature are diverse.

pmc-12372491.title: Academic global health collaboration: the Ruhuna-Duke partnership
pmc-12372491.creator: Champica K Bodinayake, Ajith De S Nagahawatte, Vijitha de Silva, P L Ariyananda, Bilesha Perera, Ruvini Kurukulasooriya, M H Madureka Premamali, Christopher W Woods, L Gayani Tillekeratne, Truls Østbye
pmc-12372491.description: The role of institutional partnerships is increasingly recognized as a means of advancing our collective efficacy in improving public health. Shared challenges related to infectious and chronic diseases, as well as social determinants of health including environmental stressors, have led to a growth in academic global health collaborations.

pmc-12374303.title: Molecular epidemiology and genomic features of Bordetella pertussis in Tianjin, China, 2023
pmc-12374303.creator: Xiaohui Lu, Wen Li, Xuan Chen, Wei Zhang, Aiping Yu, Guangwen Liu, Baolu Zheng, Xin Gao, Yamin Liu, Xiaoyan Li
pmc-12374303.description: BackgroundPertussis, a highly contagious respiratory disease caused by Bordetella pertussis (BP), poses challenges due to genomic variation that may contribute to its persistence in vaccinated populations and the development of antimicrobial resistance.MethodsIn this study, we characterized 27 BP isolates collected from Tianjin, China in 2023, using whole-genome sequencing and multilocus genotyping (MGT) to explore their genomic diversity.

pmc-12618540.title: The impact of economic complexity on green technology innovation in China
pmc-12618540.creator: Xiang Ruan, Shanlang Lin, Junpei Huang, Chenghan Li
pmc-12618540.description: Green technology innovation (GTI) plays a pivotal role in mitigating global climate change and advancing environmental sustainability. Economic complexity, which reveals the diversity and sophistication of economic structures, provides a novel analytical perspective for improving the GTI. This research explores the potential influence of economic complexity on GTI advancement.

pmc-12649919.title: The miR-125a-5p/IRF4 Axis Mediates Sodium Arsenite-Induced M2 Macrophage Polarization
pmc-12649919.creator: Yan Yu, Fan Yao, Suyuan Tong, Mingzheng Li, Qilong Liao, Fei Wang, Shuhua Xi, Chiara Moltrasio, Fabian Benencia
pmc-12649919.description: Arsenic, a ubiquitous metalloid, is commonly found in surface waters; as well as serious human health issues, it also induces systemic diseases and carcinogenesis upon chronic exposure. To better understand how arsenic potentially alters the immune system, it is important to study its effects on macrophage polarization. Micro-RNA plays an epigenetic regulatory role in organisms.

pmc-13280188.title: Engineering of Glioblastoma‐Derived Biomimetic Vesicles and Their Structural and Molecular Features
pmc-13280188.creator: Noelia Hernández‐Lobato, Hanan Abumanhal‐Masarweh, Martí de Cabo, Pablo Guerra, Marilena Hadjidemetriou, Neus Lozano, Kostas Kostarelos
pmc-13280188.description: Biomimetic nanosystems and vesicles have arisen as a novel approach to design vesicular transport systems with diverse therapeutic potential. The ‘biomimetic’ strategy involves the integration of cell membrane components into lipid bilayers, conferring them with biological properties originating from the cell of origin.

pmc-13349351.title: The Impact of Combined Vitamin D and A Supplementation on Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Pneumosepsis: A Randomized Double-Blind Clinical Trial
pmc-13349351.creator: Abolfazl Jokar, Alireza Sistani, Farshideh Didgar, Elham Niasati
pmc-13349351.description: Background:Pneumosepsis is a severe and potentially life-threatening infection of the lower respiratory tract. This study aimed to investigate the effect of combined vitamin D and A supplementation on clinical outcomes in patients with pneumosepsis.Material and Methods:Eighty-four patients with pneumosepsis were randomly assigned to four groups in this double-blind clinical trial.

pmc-13356935.title: Sex differences in imaging features including cerebral amyloid angiopathy markers in intracerebral hemorrhage
pmc-13356935.creator: Trine Apostolaki-Hansson, Christine Kremer, Amir Hillal, Cheryl Carcel, Teresa Ullberg, Bo Norrving, Jesper Petersson
pmc-13356935.description: BackgroundReports on sex differences in radiological characteristics of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) are few. Sex-related differences in hematoma location, volume, and imaging markers may contribute to variations in clinical presentation and outcome. We aimed to assess sex differences in non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) features in an unselected ICH cohort.

pmc-13392342.title: Clostridium-Derived p-Cresyl Metabolites Induce Inflammation and Apoptosis in Biliary Epithelial Cells
pmc-13392342.creator: Haiyan Yu, Haiyan Fu, Jiamin Xu, Yina Yang, Xin Ai, Rongfang Tu, Weimin Bao, Yingmei Tang

pmc-13452862.title: Analyzing audience participation at the 43rd workshop of the german surgical working group on endocrinology (CAEK): gender balance in academic discussion dynamics in endocrine surgery
pmc-13452862.creator: Anna Mikl, M Kießler, M Berlet, M Martignoni, H Friess, C Chiapponi
pmc-13452862.description: IntroductionAlthough many surgical fields remain male dominated, the rising number of female medical students and physicians raises important questions about engagement dynamics within academic and professional settings. Endocrine Surgery (ES) currently demonstrates high rates of female representation among its fellows all over the world.

pmc-13489857.title: Expert consensus recommendations for the prevention and management of immunoglobulin therapy-related adverse reactions in primary and secondary immunodeficiencies: a national Delphi study from the Immunodeficiency Group of the Spanish Society of Immunology
pmc-13489857.creator: Andrea Ferranti-Ramos, Marta Aguilar-Criado, Carmen L. Avendaño-Monje, María de las Mercedes Díaz Luna, Cinthya M. Fusi-Velarde, Jaime Pons
pmc-13489857.description: IntroductionHuman immunoglobulin (IG) therapy, administered intravenously (IVIG) or subcutaneously (SCIG), is a cornerstone treatment for primary and secondary immunodeficiencies (PID and SID) and is increasingly used in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Although generally safe, adverse drug reactions (ADR) may affect treatment adherence, patient safety, and quality of care. Practical recommendations for the prevention and management of IG-associated ADR remain limited.
